subtype: Approach: looking at the ground right in front of the wheel [Pitfall]
passage:
Jaya: Asif, watch me! I'll go round the pole.
Asif: Don't look at the tyre. Look... never mind.
Jaya: I have to see where the wheel goes!
Asif: The pole is right there!
Jaya: I know it's there. That's why I'm watching it. Oh no, oh no...
Asif: Turn! Turn!
The cycle wobbled straight into the pole, and Jaya sat down hard on the ground.
Jaya: Ow! Why did it go straight at the pole?
Asif: You stared at it the whole way.
Jaya rubbed her scraped knee and did not laugh. The helmet had slid over one eye.

qa.q: What did Jaya want to do with the pole?
qa.a: Jaya wanted to go round the pole.

qa.q: What was Jaya feeling as she wobbled toward the pole?
qa.a: Jaya was scared and flustered; the repeated 'oh no' shows fear as the cycle drifted toward the pole.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Jaya use next time, and why?
qa.a: Jaya could look at the open space where she wants to go instead of the pole. Eyes tend to steer the hands toward where they look.

qa.q: How does Asif see what went wrong?
qa.a: Asif could see the pole ahead and the way Jaya stared at it, and tried to warn her, so Asif probably feels worried and a little helpless watching it happen.

grounding: A child stares at the front tyre and the pole she wants to avoid, then wobbles into the pole and pays with a scraped knee.

subtype: Approach: looking at the ground right in front of the wheel [Pitfall]
passage: Last week I found out my eyes can steer a cycle. Our lane has one electricity pole right in the middle, and I was so scared of hitting it that I kept staring down at my front tyre, watching it wobble over every stone. The pole got closer at the edge of my eye. I kept thinking, don't hit it, don't hit it. Then bang. My handlebar hit the pole and I scraped my shin on the pedal. My little brother Vaibhav ran over yelling, "Vandana didi, you were looking right at it!" He was right. Whatever I was scared of, my wheel went straight there. Now I have a plaster, a sore shin, and I still don't like that pole.

qa.q: What did Vandana scrape when the handlebar hit the pole?
qa.a: Vandana scraped a shin on the pedal.

qa.q: What was Vandana feeling as the pole got closer?
qa.a: Vandana was scared and tense, repeating "don't hit it", and that fear kept pulling the eyes and wheel toward the pole.

qa.q: What else could Vandana try on the lane next time, and why?
qa.a: Vandana could look at the gate or a tree beyond the pole, because hands tend to steer where the eyes point.

qa.q: How did the crash look to Vaibhav?
qa.a: Vaibhav could see what Vandana could not: that the eyes were fixed on the pole, so it looked obvious and a little funny to him 😅

grounding: It shows a child who stares at the tyre and then at a feared pole, and wobbles straight into it.

subtype: Approach: looking at the ground right in front of the wheel [Pitfall]
passage:
Coach's note, Saturday learners' group, park track
Gurpreet rode her second full lap today but kept her chin tucked and her eyes glued to the front tyre. At the bend there is a lamp pole I had pointed out to the group. She said aloud, "I won't hit it, I won't hit it," glanced up at the pole, and her handlebars drifted right toward it. She clipped it and fell onto the grass: one scraped palm, no other injury. She was shaken and cross with herself. After we cleaned the scrape, I set two orange cones past the bend and asked her to look only at them. She managed one slow bend without drifting. Next week the whole group will start with the cones drill.
- Tanuja, coach

qa.q: What did Tanuja set past the bend after cleaning the scrape?
qa.a: Tanuja set two orange cones past the bend.

qa.q: What was Gurpreet feeling after she clipped the pole?
qa.a: She was shaken and cross with herself, because she had been trying so hard not to hit it.

qa.q: Which approach suits Gurpreet better, and why?
qa.a: Looking at a target past the danger, like the cones, suits her better, because her steering follows her eyes rather than her fear.

qa.q: What is it like for the coach to watch Gurpreet drift toward the pole?
qa.a: The coach can see the mistake coming but cannot stop it in time, so it is worrying, and it shapes next week's drill for everyone.

grounding: It shows a child who fixes her eyes near the tyre and on the pole she fears, and is pulled into it.
